title: Reuse shared configuration in a pooled factory
goal: Compose a pooled factory with shared ConfigureDbContext settings while disposing leases and clearing request state.

selectionNotes: Register shared configuration with Singleton lifetime before resolving the factory. EF11 adds the overload without an options callback. The maximum retained pool size defaults to 1024; the sample sets 1 to make sequential reuse observable. Dispose every factory-created context. EF resets tracking; application fields need explicit cleanup in both Dispose and DisposeAsync. RequestLabel is cleared before returning the lease. Do not capture scoped services in shared options or put provider setup in OnConfiguring. Do not use a context concurrently or after disposal. Context pooling is separate from driver connection pooling. This synchronous example is not a general tenant-isolation or connection-session-state guarantee.

EF10 already consumes shared ConfigureDbContext settings with Singleton lifetime. AddPooledDbContextFactory still requires a callback; the measured older route supplies an empty callback. Keeping that callback remains valid in EF11. Removing registration boilerplate does not establish automatic application-state reset.

Supported current route requires .NET/SDK11 and matching EF11 SQLite packages. Measured: SDK11.0.100, runtime11 RC3, C#15 and EF11.0.0; previous: SDK10.0.403, runtime10.0.14, C#14 and EF10.0.13. Stable API shapes measured on RC2 are not GA verification. No experimental opt-in or C#15-specific syntax is required. EF11 requires net11.0 although direct SQLite11 selects net10.0; no older-runtime EF11 route or extra .NET10 foundation is offered. Windows x64 executes SQLite3.53.3/SQLitePCLRaw2.1.13 versus SQLite3.53.4/SQLitePCLRaw3.0.5 using normal e_sqlite3 initialization. Full independent graphs and content hashes are locked. No encryption, retired bundle, other provider/platform or production guarantee. No workload or browser rendering mode applies. The fixture owns its open in-memory connection until all contexts and service providers are disposed. Never share a context concurrently.
prerequisites: Copy complete canonical projects into separate directories. Restore pinned packages before offline execution. Disposable in-memory SQLite only. No credentials, account or external resources.
stabilityLimitations: Stable API shape in GA-targeted guidance, measured on RC2 packages and SDK. No experimental API suppression required. Actual GA reconciliation remains outstanding.

evidence.scope: Run eng/Test-WrenTracking.ps1 to execute both locked graphs; -Record refreshes sample verification-evidence.json. Records contain exact commands, SDK/runtime details, resolved dependencies, input hashes, host, SQLite version/source ID, executed SQL and PASS checks. This is actual compilation and SQLite execution, not mocks, metadata or cross-compilation. State checks cover stale/current states, all flags/defaults, scan counts and persisted insert/update/delete. Scalar checks cover partial SELECT, UPDATE omission, fresh reload, re-enable/default write and loaded update. Pool checks cover shared configuration, disposal/reuse, EF tracking and explicit RequestLabel reset, unsaved-mutation exclusion and persisted save. Other application fields and async interaction are not independently exercised. Ordinary installed-tool inspection separately checks ID/title/goal, complete canonical Markdown, target11/edition11, applicability and evidence over real stdio from an unrelated directory with unusable proxies. That proves embedded retrieval, not OS network isolation. PIN-959 comprehensive coverage, PIN-965 actual GA and existing Human gates remain open. Each M(3) retains its focused correctness/lifecycle and consumer proof scope; no recurring platform/client matrix is added.
